title: Lower degree bound for a finite graded polynomial module
statement: Let k be a field, S=k[x_0,x_1] with its total-degree grading [def-sc-p1-standard], and N a finitely generated S-module with an internal additive direct sum decomposition N=⊕_{j∈ℤ} N_j. Assume S_t N_j⊆N_{t+j} for every natural number t. There exists B∈ℤ such that every x∈N_j with j<B is zero.

proof.text: Choose a finite family of homogeneous generators m_i with degrees d_i, via the surjective linear map from the finitely supported free module supplied by [lem-sc-p1-finite-homogeneous-generators].

source.place: proof: graded Hilbert syzygy theorem; standard graded Nakayama argument expanded in lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-generation, not explicit in the blueprint

proof.text: Choose a lower bound B for the finite set of degrees d_i; a lower bound also exists when the family is empty. Decompose each polynomial coefficient into its finitely many homogeneous components. A degree-t component multiplied by m_i has degree t+d_i≥B. Its projection to a degree j<B vanishes by internal direct-sum independence. Additivity and surjectivity show that the degree-j component of every element of N is zero. For x∈N_j that component equals x, so x=0.

theorem exists_graded_module_lower_bound {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {N : Type v} [AddCommGroup N] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) N]
    [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) N]
    (ℳ : ℤ → AddSubgroup N) (hℳ : DirectSum.IsInternal ℳ)
    (hsmul : ∀ (t : ℕ) (j : ℤ) (s : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (x : N),
      s ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k t → x ∈ ℳ j →
        s • x ∈ ℳ ((t : ℤ) + j)) :
    ∃ B : ℤ, ∀ (j : ℤ) (x : N), j < B → x ∈ ℳ j → x = 0
